question: What marine fish and crustacean evidence does the official 2019 MCTEP Segment 5 EIS report for its Cavite coastal sampling, and can any listed fish be assigned specifically to Julugan, Tanza or Tanza Marine Tree Park?

method.summary: Reviewed Section 2.2.5.1, Figure 2.54, Table 2.27, and Figure 2.55 in the public EMB-hosted EIS text view. Compared the narrative site/method description, executive-summary totals, printed taxonomic rows, and chart-level genus labels. The freshwater tables in the same EIS were reviewed separately in the parent artifact. No PDF, map image, or specimen photo was copied into the repository.
method.samplingContext: The EIS names three marine-fish collection contexts: Wakas II, Kawit; Rosario Municipal Fish Port; and Julugan, Tanza. It says fish and crustaceans were collected at the Rosario landing site and from fishermen fishing in municipal waters about 15 km from shore at Kawit and Tanza. The map labels Julugan, Tanza as Site 3. The table is explicitly pooled across all sites and has no species-by-site, exact capture coordinate, individual specimen/voucher identifier, gear, or fish-specific collection date crosswalk.
method.dateCaution: The EIS separately dates a six-station water-quality survey to 25 January 2018. The reviewed marine fish section does not state that date as the fish-collection date, so it is not assigned to the fish samples.
method.rightsAndImages: No item-specific permission or open license to reuse the EIS table, map, or specimen photos was verified. Printed specimen photos were not retained or treated as independently taxon-validated Bangwit species images.
method.dietCaution: The EIS includes generalized habitat and feeding descriptions attributed to reference literature. They are not local stomach-content observations, bait tests, or evidence of what the Cavite specimens ate; no diet or bait guidance is derived from them.

countAndIdentityIssues: The executive summary reports 17 fish species in 17 families, while Table 2.27 has 18 fish rows. The 18 rows include both Sphyraena jello and a separate Sphyraena sp. row; the source does not reconcile this count difference.
Table 2.27 has three crustacean rows; its labels should not be counted as fish species.
Several source spellings need an independent name-authority check. This review preserves them as printed and does not infer corrected specimen identities.
Figure 2.55 displays genus-level labels and a pooled relative-abundance chart. It does not provide a fish species-by-site or locality crosswalk.
findings.parkLink: The EIS names Julugan, Tanza as one of three pooled coastal fish-collection contexts. It does not name Tanza Marine Tree Park or establish that any sample came from the park, its mangroves, or a specific station within municipal waters.
findings.speciesPhotos: The EIS contains some specimen photos in Table 2.27, but no photo was independently matched to a taxon and no item-level reuse right was established. Do not reuse them as Bangwit species reference images.

decision.disposition: Retain the 18 printed fish rows and 3 crustacean rows as one historical pooled Cavite municipal-fisheries research lead, not as Tanza-specific or Tanza Marine Tree Park occurrences. Preserve raw taxon spellings pending independent name and specimen review.

nonClaims: The EIS does not assign any Table 2.27 fish taxon to Julugan, Tanza, Wakas II, Kawit, or the Rosario fish landing site individually.
A Tanza place-name and municipal-water sampling description do not establish a TMTP capture, a surveyed station point, or a legal municipal-water boundary.
The fish-collection date, gear, individual voucher repository, and item-specific reuse permission remain unverified in the reviewed section.
The source's general feeding descriptions do not establish local diet, natural prey observations, bait effectiveness, or catch advice.
No current presence, abundance, safety, fishing access, legality, or complete Cavite/Manila Bay checklist is established.
nextActions: Cross-check the exact fish and crustacean source spellings against current authoritative taxonomic catalogs while preserving the original strings and the EIS family labels.
Keep the table held from app projection until species identity, station/site linkage, provenance, and item-specific reuse are resolved.

Continue searching for an independently reusable, dated fish survey with per-site species, gear, coordinates, and traceable vouchers; keep Tanza Marine Tree Park separate from Julugan and other Tanza coastal localities.

sources.supports: Official EMB-hosted 2019 MCTEP Segment 5 EIS marine fish-collection narrative, Figure 2.54, Table 2.27, Figure 2.55, and the previously reviewed freshwater section.
